{"kind":"proof","text":"Since \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb R\), the inverse image \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). Moreover,
\[
f^{-1}(\{0\})=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=Z(f).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed.","reason":"A continuous function has closed inverse images of closed sets, and the zero set is precisely the inverse image of the closed singleton \(\{0\}\)."}
